title: Restic fails to refresh locks under linux kernel 6.1 with default huge pages settings
body:
Output of `restic version`
--------------------------
`restic 0.15.0 compiled with go1.19.5 on linux/amd64`

How did you run restic exactly?
-------------------------------
`restic backup --one-file-system --tag ${tag} ${path}`

Environment variables set:
```
RESTIC_REPOSITORY=b2:${uuid}
RESTIC_CACHE_DIR=${path_to_cache_dir}
RESTIC_COMPRESSION=max
RESTIC_PASSWORD_FILE=${CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY}/password
B2_ACCOUNT_ID=${account_id}
B2_ACCOUNT_KEY=${account_key}
DEBUG_FILES=lock.go  # added for debugging
```

Output (including timestamps from the system log)
```
Jan 16 21:45:41: debug enabled
Jan 16 21:45:55: restic/lock.go:50        main.lockRepository        1        create lock 0xc00018e7e0 (exclusive false)
Jan 16 21:45:55: restic/lock.go:75        main.refreshLocks        166        start
Jan 16 21:45:56: using parent snapshot ed3543b1
Jan 16 21:50:55: restic/lock.go:105        main.refreshLocks        166        refreshing locks
Jan 16 21:50:55: restic/lock.go:234        restic.(*Lock).Refresh        166        refreshing lock 12ab00c6
Jan 16 22:08:26: Fatal: failed to refresh lock in time
Jan 16 22:08:26: error: no result
Jan 16 22:08:26: error: no result
Jan 16 22:08:26: error: no result
Jan 16 22:08:26: error: no result
Jan 16 22:08:26: error: no result
Jan 16 22:08:33: restic/lock.go:246        restic.(*Lock).Refresh        166        new lock ID a978291194edde410982cd82cde86370a9dcf42cebccc73ea004af8612a184c0
Jan 16 22:08:38: restic/lock.go:97        main.refreshLocks        166        terminate
Jan 16 22:08:38: restic/lock.go:85        main.refreshLocks.func1        166        unlocking repository with lock PID 70825 on starlight by root (UID 0, GID 0)
Jan 16 22:08:38: lock was created at 2023-01-16 21:50:55 (17m43.186891971s ago)
Jan 16 22:08:38: storage ID a9782911
Jan 16 22:08:40: Fatal: unable to save snapshot: context canceled
Jan 16 22:08:40: restic/lock.go:181        main.unlockAll        1        unlocking 0 locks
```

What backend/server/service did you use to store the repository?
----------------------------------------------------------------
The Backblaze b2 backend

Expected behavior
-----------------
The backup should complete successfully

Actual behavior
---------------
The backup fails with the log messages above after ~22m 30s. The proximate cause seems to be #2715 which makes operations bail out if they fail to refresh their locks for too long (where too long = 22m 30s), but this may just be revealing a pre-existing issue. While running restic spends a while before failing with all threads in an interruptible sleep (observed through `top`), and it fails promptly once the timer expires, so it doesn't seem to be deadlocked or starved for resources. I observe that on this run the lock was successfully refreshed once, but this doesn't seem to have pushed out the failure at all. This could possibly be explained if the lock refresh itself hung.

Steps to reproduce the behavior
-------------------------------
This has happened on all my backup runs since upgrading to 0.15

Do you have any idea what may have caused this?
-----------------------------------------------
While upgrading I replaced my application key with a key that lacks delete permissions, as enabled by #2134. It seems possible to me that a bug there would cause something like this. I haven't yet tried going back to a key with delete permissions since it would be a pain to do.

Did restic help you today? Did it make you happy in any way?
------------------------------------------------------------
I really liked the new support for using the b2 backend without delete permissions

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Okay, on further investigation what seems to be happening is that I misconfigured how bandwidth is allocated between multiple uploaders with the effect that restic got only a very small slice of traffic. This results in pack uploads taking so long the lock becomes stale, and because there are no free semaphore tokens it can't be refreshed, eventually causing the command to fail.

This is clearly mostly my fault, but it would be good if restic output a more useful error message in this case.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Giving restic more bandwidth made this failure less frequent, but didn't actually eliminate it, and it now sometimes happens after 10s of minutes or hours of work (a typical successful backup takes ~10 minutes to run) so I'm going to re-open this.

I also recently saw this issue in `restic forget --prune` (I didn't have debug logs enabled)
```

Jan 22 18:25:46 starlight restic.py[206907]: loading indexes...
Jan 22 18:55:18 starlight restic.py[206907]: Fatal: failed to refresh lock in time
Jan 22 18:55:23 starlight restic.py[206907]: loading all snapshots...
Jan 22 18:55:25 starlight restic.py[206907]: Fatal: failed loading snapshot: context canceled
```
Loading the indexes and snapshots should, IIUC, mostly hit the local cache, so I'm surprised that updating the repository lock could be blocked.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Further investigation with strace reveals that these huge pauses occur in mmap syscalls. Turning off [transparent huge pages](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/mm/transhuge.html) in sysfs seems to resolve the issue, so I suspect the go runtime is requesting use of huge pages in a way that causes pathological performance with the default kernel settings. I suspect the setting to change is `/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/defrag` which defaults to blocking new allocations in regions marked with `MADV_HUGEPAGE` (frequently requested by the go runtime) while memory is defragmented. Setting this to `never` (effectively ignore `MADV_HUGEPAGE`) or `defer` (only try to defragment memory in the background, rather than blocking the allocating process) likely also works.

I'm inclined to close this, since this is at a lower level then restic itself is written at, but it would also be good if this was reasonably discoverable for anyone having a similar issue and I'm not sure how to effectuate that.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I wonder why defragmenting memory to assemble a huge page should be that slow. After all it shouldn't be necessary to collect more than 2MB at a time. Is the system maybe short on free memory?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Most of the memory usage was filesystem cache, which should be free to discard, and would also have been the case previously.

Tracing back through my system logs I can see this didn't actually regress when I installed restic 0.15, that just introduced the loud failure when the underlying issue did happen. That makes sense since go's default usage of huge pages seems to have last been touched back in 2019 with [this commit](https://github.com/golang/go/commit/31c4e099158b0e4999c05ee4daf08531f6640ad4), and nothing relevant changed in restic. The issue seems to have _actually_ started when I upgraded to kernel version 6.1.1 from 6.0.12, which is presumably a bug in the kernel. Doing some quick searches turns up some recent huge-pages-related patches on the lkml, so I would tentatively guess one of them introduced this regression.
